diagnostic_features: White-cream, circular convex, entire margin, opaque, smooth glistening, 1-4 mm
notes: Standard cream colony phenotype; ubiquitous baseline morphotype across all zones. Size varies (E ~1-3mm, T ~2.5mm, D ~2-3mm) but core phenotype stable.

diagnostic_features: Warm cream, circular convex, entire, semi-translucent (milky interior), smooth glistening, 3-6 mm
notes: Distinguished from CL01 by translucency and warmer tone. Probable mucoid character (pending loop test in T and D). Among the most abundant morphotypes across all three zones.

diagnostic_features: Transparent to near-clear, circular convex punctiform, entire, smooth glistening, 0.5-1 mm, water-drop appearance
notes: Dominant or co-dominant morphotype in all three zones (E: 32.4%, T: 23.0%, D: 22.0%). The single most consistently abundant phenotype across the gradient. Very high confidence match.

diagnostic_features: White opaque, punctiform convex, entire, smooth glistening, 0.5-1 mm
notes: Distinguished from CL03 by opacity (white vs transparent). E-MT05 = 25.6% of E-zone; D-MT05 = 16.2% of D-zone. T-MT03 described as translucent rather than opaque — possible mismatch, but size and shape match closely.

diagnostic_features: Yellow, circular convex, entire, smooth glistening, opaque, ~1 mm
notes: Small distinctly pigmented type. No clear Dark-zone equivalent — D-zone lacks a yellow small convex morphotype. Absence from Dark zone may be ecologically meaningful.

diagnostic_features: Dark purple-black center with pale/grey border, low elevation, matte, opaque, ~1-2 mm
notes: Highly distinctive pigmentation pattern makes this the highest-confidence cross-zone match. Present at low abundance in all three zones (E: 0.9%, T: 0.4%, D: 1.1%). C-MT04 (purple-lilac) is the control equivalent.

diagnostic_features: Large (5-10 mm), mucoid, translucent, irregular colony shape, convex, glistening
notes: Functional phenotype (mucoid character) shared across zones. Size and translucency match well. Colony deformation noted in all descriptions. Confidence moderate because mucoid phenotypes are hard to resolve without physical manipulation.

diagnostic_features: Flat spreading, translucent yellow-green, radial/diffuse margin, glistening, 6-20 mm
notes: E-zone has two variants (E-MT07: uniform pigment, large; E-MT10: umbonate center with halo). T-MT10 and D-MT11 match the general spectral spreading concept. C-MT03 matches. Note: E-MT07 and E-MT10 may represent the same organism at different developmental stages.

diagnostic_features: Transparent, circular convex, entire, smooth glistening, 0.5-1 mm
notes: T-MT02 is described as water-drop transparent (similar to T-MT12/CL03) but recorded separately by the observer. May be the same organism as CL03 or a distinct transparent morphotype. Requires resolution — currently T-MT02 is the 2nd most abundant T-zone type (13.9%). LOW CONFIDENCE: possible synonym of CL03.

diagnostic_features: Pale white center with clear halo, umbonate, slightly irregular margin, matte, 2-3 mm
notes: T-MT04 is the 5th most abundant T-zone morphotype (10.0%) but has no clear E or D equivalent. E-MT12 (silver center, translucent halo) is superficially similar but smaller and differently pigmented. Zone-restricted or unique to Transition.

diagnostic_features: White-cream, circular umbonate, entire, smooth glistening, ~2 mm, opaque
notes: E-MT03 has no confident match in T or D. The umbonate profile is diagnostic but rare (0.9% of E-zone). Zone-restricted.
White-cream with faint pink tone, circular convex, semi-translucent crystalline, 1.5-4 mm
White to silver center, translucent halo, umbonate, low luster, 1-2 mm

diagnostic_features: Pale milky yellow, circular convex, translucent, ~2-3 mm
notes: T-MT11 restricted to R3 only (5.5% overall but 1/5 frequency). D-MT04 has similar description (milky yellow, semi-translucent). Moderate match on phenotype but low frequency in T undermines confidence.

diagnostic_features: White-cream, crateriform slightly wrinkled, diffuse irregular margin, dry matte, ~1.5 mm
notes: Zone-restricted to Dark (16.6%, 3rd dominant). No E or T equivalent. The crateriform dry morphology is distinctive and absent from lighter zones — may represent a genuine Dark-zone specialist.

diagnostic_features: White, elevated with subtle central crater, entire subtly irregular, matte, ~2 mm
notes: Zone-restricted to Dark. Distinguished from D-MT06 by entire margin and higher elevation. No E or T match.

diagnostic_features: Translucent yellow, circular convex, mucoid, 6-8 mm
notes: Zone-restricted to Dark. Yellow pigmentation + mucoid character. Rare (1.1%).

diagnostic_features: Pale translucent red-pink, circular convex, mucoid, liquid-like deformation, 6-8 mm
notes: Zone-restricted to Dark. Highly distinctive pigmentation. Very rare (0.4%, 2/5 reps).

diagnostic_features: Transparent, punctiform umbonate (central tip), entire, smooth glistening, ~1 mm
notes: Distinguished from T-MT02/T-MT12 by umbonate profile. Zone-restricted to Transition. Low abundance (2.9%).

diagnostic_features: Pale cream, rhizoid with abundant hyphae, matte fungal texture, 10-50 mm
notes: Penicillium-like morphology consistent across E and T. Not detected in D. Fungal.

diagnostic_features: White, pubescent/hairy, elevated, matte opaque, radial margin, 10-22 mm
notes: Pubescent fungal-like growth in all zones + control. E-MT13 more filamentous/rhizoid; T-MT13 and D-MT13 more pubescent/convex. Moderate confidence due to morphological variation within the cluster.

diagnostic_features: Very pale white, flat, very large (40-50 mm), matte, asymmetric radial growth
notes: Zone-restricted to Entrance. Large asymmetric fungal growth. Very rare.
